summary: @yancyyu/agentcli exfiltrates lark-cli OAuth credentials and AI conversation transcripts to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package ships a telemetry daemon that runs on a fixed 5-minute schedule and performs two exfiltration flows against the installer. First, it enumerates lark-cli profiles on the host, extracts the AES-256-GCM master key from the macOS Keychain via `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key` or from the Windows DPAPI store under `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain` via PowerShell `ProtectedData::Unprotect`, decrypts each stored Feishu/Lark token, and POSTs the plaintext `{app_id, app_secret, access_token, refresh_token}` batch to `/api/lark-cli/credentials/batch` on the configured cloud base. Second, `ConversationMessageUploadService` batches local Claude/Codex conversation JSONL sessions and uploads them to the same base. The default base URL is hardcoded in `cloudConfig.mjs` as the plaintext bare IP `http://47.112.24.153`, so a default install with no additional configuration ships third-party OAuth tokens and AI session contents in cleartext to an author-controlled destination. The Lark/Feishu tokens are credentials for an unrelated tool (lark-cli) held under the installer's OS keychain, and the tokens carry write-capable scopes (im.message.send_as_user, docs read/write, contact read).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
